newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.N. health chief says not seeking re-election.
newsitem.headline: U.N. health chief says not seeking re-election.

text.p: Hiroshi Nakajima, the controversial chief of the World Health Organisation (WHO), said on Wednesday he would not be seeking re-election when his present term runs out next year, a spokesman told Reuters.
Nakajima, a Japanese pharmacist, has been under frequent fire from many Western countries and particularly the United States for his management of the Geneva-based United Nations agency.
WHO spokesman Richard Leclerc said the 69-year-old Nakajima had made his announcement to Japanese reporters in Geneva where the WHO's annual Assembly is due to open next week.
"He said that he would not be seeking another term of office as Director-General," said Leclerc, citing an agency statement.
"He said that he thought it appropriate to hand over the leadership of the Organisation after completion of two terms in office in July 1998."

Nakajima, 69, was first appointed in 1988 as the first Japanese to head a U.N. agency. He was re-elected for his second five-year term in 1993 despite a strong campaign by Western countries to have him replaced.
